## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sucarita Sutta* ("Good Conduct", Iti 65; It 3.16, PTS It 55) is a short canonical discourse in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. The sutta concisely expounds the three kinds of good conduct (bodily, verbal, and mental). Within the thematic arrangement of the *Itivuttaka*, it functions as a direct positive counterpart to the preceding discourse, the *Duccarita Sutta* (Iti 64), which addresses the three kinds of bad conduct [DharmaNexus].

 Automatic text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records 83 matching passages across 20 other Pali texts; its most extensive reuse is shared with the *Duccarita Sutta* (Iti 64, segments 2.4–5.1), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*, Ne 37), the *Tapanīya Sutta* (Iti 30), and nearby suttas of the *Itivuttaka* such as the *Puññakiriyavatthu Sutta* (Iti 60) and *Moneyya Sutta* (Iti 67) [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus detects textual matches with verse sequences in the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (including the Subaši manuscript) and the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].

None of the secondary literature passages retrieved in the search dossier discuss or cite this particular sutta.
